question: A couple has a child with Down syndrome confirmed on karyotype showing 47,XY,+21. Parental karyotypes are both normal. The paediatrician counsels them that recurrence risk is primarily driven by maternal age and is approximately 1%. Which cytogenetic mechanism in the child explains this recurrence estimate?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Robertsonian translocation results from fusion of chromosome 21 with chromosome 14. When a parent carries the balanced translocation, recurrence risk rises to 10–15% (carrier mother) or ~5% (carrier father) — much higher than the maternal-age-dependent 1% figure. Parental karyotyping is mandatory when translocation is found in the child.

Free (non-disjunction) trisomy 21 accounts for ~95% of Down syndrome cases. With normal parental karyotypes, the recurrence risk is approximately 1% above the maternal-age-related background risk — the figure quoted in this scenario. Karyotype is 47,XX,+21 or 47,XY,+21.

Mosaic Down syndrome results from non-disjunction in an early post-zygotic mitotic division, giving two cell lines (46 and 47). It accounts for ~1–2% of cases and generally has the same low maternal-age-dependent recurrence as free trisomy. However, the karyotype here shows 47,XY,+21 in all cells — not a mosaic pattern.

answers.text: Partial trisomy 21 due to a de novo inversion

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Partial trisomy 21 (due to duplications or inversions) is rare and would not yield the classic 47,XY,+21 karyotype. It is not one of the three main cytogenetic types described for Down syndrome.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the three mechanisms of Down syndrome: (1) free trisomy 21 — non-disjunction, ~95%, normal parental karyotype, recurrence ~1%; (2) Robertsonian translocation t(14;21) — ~4%, parental karyotype essential, higher recurrence; (3) mosaicism — ~1–2%, post-zygotic mitotic error.

Correct. Free trisomy 21 (non-disjunction, ~95%) gives a normal parental karyotype and a maternal-age-related recurrence of ~1%. Robertsonian translocation and mosaicism have different mechanisms and counselling implications.
